_doc: Simple model: will Tesla announce its 2026 annual meeting, (A) with a merger or (B) routine, between window.start and window.end? Edit and rerun update.py.

p_any_by_end._why: Base case: Tesla holds its 2026 annual meeting in 2026 (~95%), which forces a date announcement before the notice cutoffs (e-proxy ~Oct 27, Texas 10-day ~Nov 26 for a Dec 6 meeting). The remaining ~5% is Tesla slipping to 2027. The Texas 13-month rule (BOC 21.351) is enforceable only by a shareholder court petition, so slipping is possible but unlikely.

a_share._why: Starting 50/50 for WITH merger vs routine before evidence. The merger thesis and a Sept 18 outside read lean merger; Polymarket's Dec 31 2026 contract (~14%) leans routine. The leak decay and the signals adjust it.

signals.label: SEC retail standing-instruction no-action letter (Sept 29). Downgraded: holders can choose 'all matters except mergers', and anyone who chose 'all matters' gets a reminder and can override before a merger vote
$30B credit 8-K (Sept 29): rules out 'waiting on an equity raise' as the reason, neutral for a merger
SpaceX-Grain 800 MHz deal (Oct 8, ~$8B cash per WSJ, pending FCC): adds more Tesla-relevant connectivity
Terafab or Optimus Gen 3 event date set with no meeting or letter (flip on)
Roadster goes cleanly (Oct 15) and still no meeting date (flip on Oct 16 if true)
Special committee, banker, counsel or 'people familiar' deal report (flip on; also resets the leak decay)
Tesla says the meeting slips to 2027 with no date (flip on)
Barclays (Dan Levy) note, Oct 14: merger announcement possible before the annual meeting (by Dec 6). Named sell-side coverage, no new facts; small judgment bump (+1.5 pts merger, any path)

urgency.label: Tesla's usual 40-45 day DEF 14A lead puts the latest on-time proxy (Dec 6 meeting) here
A mid/late-Dec meeting still fits Tesla's usual 40-45 day lead
Last chance for any 2026 meeting (Texas 10-day minimum)

weekday_mult._why: Monday most likely (Sunday-night/pre-market filings count as Monday), Tuesday a close second, small weekend share.

blackouts.label: Roadster demo (evening)
blackouts._event_note: Roadster livestream 8:55 PM ET; end = start + ~2.5h (not published)
blackouts._why: Roadster event day relaxed from x0.3 to x1.4 (Oct 14): the day stays open to the event end (11:25 PM ET) and covers a morning filing plus an on-stage/X comment after the livestream (8-K next morning counts as this day). Targets ~2% for the day.

blackouts.label: Q3 earnings after the close
blackouts._event_note: Q3 call 5:30 PM ET; 8 PM close still applies

post_event_boost.label: Clean-Monday boost (Oct 19)
post_event_boost._why: First clean Monday after the Oct 15 Roadster event and before Tesla's Oct 21 earnings; early enough that a shareholder letter would not collide with the earnings call. Named per-date multiplier on both merger and routine paths.

notice_rules.detail: Notice of Internet Availability must go out 40+ calendar days before the meeting. Tesla used notice and access in 2025 (mailed Sept 17 for Nov 6).
Written notice 10 to 60 days before the meeting.
If there's no annual meeting within 13 months, a shareholder who made a written request can ask a court to order one. Missing it does not dissolve the company.
A routine annual meeting (directors, auditor, 14a-8 proposals) needs no preliminary proxy. Other items need a PRE 14A at least 10 days before the definitive proxy.

A vote where Tesla holders get SpaceX shares needs a Form S-4 declared effective first, and SEC review usually takes 2-4+ months. So a merger cannot be voted at a Dec 2026 meeting. Case A means the merger is announced now and voted at a 2027 special meeting, or the annual meeting is set alongside a merger announcement. (S-4 timing is general practice, not a rule citation.)

market_watch._doc: watch.py alerts (type market_move) when a contract's usable price moves >= move_pp vs ~window_hours earlier (or the oldest stored point if history is shorter). Re-alerts only after another move_pp from the last alerted price. Usable price: bid/ask mid if spread <= max_spread; else last trade if 24h volume >= min_volume_24h; else the quote is marked thin and never alerts.

alerts.rule: Alert when the news-driven part of a change is nonzero, or a watched SEC form is filed. Time decay never alerts.

timing_anchors._why: ~87% by Nov 13 when the total is 95%
~94.5% by Nov 26, the last Texas 10-day notice day for Dec 6

_timing_doc: Cumulative 'either' odds are pinned to timing_anchors (as a share of p_any_by_end). Within each segment, probability is spread by day weight (weekday x urgency x blackouts). The merger/routine split per day uses a_share with A-only blackouts.

leak_decay._why: The blank-week clock starts Mon Sept 21, 2026. That is the first Monday after the anniversary of last year's DEF 14A (Sept 17, 2025) passed with no 2026 date. Sept 29 (the retail-program letter) was considered and rejected: the program was a reason the date might wait, so the clock would start too late. The penalty is -0.13 log-odds per full blank week, capped at -1.20. It replaces the old flat 'no leaks' -0.40, which was already about 3 weeks x -0.13 on Oct 13, so nothing is double-counted. The penalty, and the lead-day suppression (x0.35 within 7 days, x0.70 for days 8-14), are scaled by the active-process share of the merger-hold reasons. The quiet-hold path ('Musk told the board to hold the date; no committee or bankers yet') wouldn't leak, so it isn't penalized. Everything turns off when committee_or_leak is on.

tranches.label: 2nd full Nasdaq trading day after SpaceX's own Q3 results (not Tesla's Oct 21 report): 28% of 180-day group
tranches.note: UNCONFIRMED. 424B4: "The second full trading day on Nasdaq immediately following the public release of our quarterly financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 — Up to 1.3 billion shares... representing 28% of the shares subject to the 180-day lock-up period." SpaceX has not set its Q3 date (no 8-K as of Oct 13). Nov 5 is a placeholder from the Aug 4 Q2 release timing and creates no blackout until confirmed.

tranches.label: After Q4 results: extended group
tranches.note: date depends on the Q4 release (~Feb/Mar)

tranches.label: Day 366 (Jun 12 Sat): extended group, plus Musk's 6.42B shares

starship._why: NET Nov 8 comes from planning-grade sources: the CADENA air-traffic planning slides of Oct 8 (cited by Wikipedia), and NASASpaceflight reporting on Oct 10 plus Musk's '4-6 weeks' remark (per thelaunchwindow). SpaceX hasn't announced a date, and Launch Library lists it only as NET Q4 2026. Unverified. Merger odds: launch day x0.1 and the day after x0.3. After a success, days +2 to +4 get x1.3. After a failure, days +1 to +5 get x0.2. The status comes from data/events_state.json (set by watch.py or by hand) or from this config.

historical_lags.src: SEC EDGAR filing index for Tesla (CIK 1318605)
historical_lags._why: Before 2025, Tesla's first public notice of the meeting date was the proxy itself (no separate date 8-K). The DEF 14A went out 40-45 days before the meeting, right at the notice-and-access minimum, and Tesla has never used the full Texas 60-day window. When there were non-routine items, a PRE 14A came about 10-13 days earlier. 2025 was the outlier: a separate 8-K on Jul 10, 119 days ahead.
historical_lags.note: Meeting dates come from the proxy filenames and well-known dates. 2020 (proxy May 28 for Jul 7) is left out because that meeting was later moved (unverified here).

blank_reasons._why: Why is the 2026 meeting still unscheduled? Weights are set as of the clock start (Sept 21) and normalized. Each full blank week multiplies the active-process weight by x0.90 (processes leak), the quiet-hold weight by x0.98, and drift by x1.04.

items.label: Merger process under way (committee or advisers working quietly)
items.note: No committee, bank or law firm disclosed as of {checked} (EDGAR and news watcher).

items.label: Musk asked the board to hold the date; no committee or bankers yet
items.note: Low leak surface: explains the blank page without a leak. Speculative path; no public evidence either way.

Pairing with a product date (Roadster Oct 15, Optimus Gen 3)
items.note: Roadster demo Oct 15 (Tesla). No Optimus Gen 3 date announced as of {checked} (news watcher).

items.label: New comp/governance item being prepared
items.note: Cut from 20%. Searches turned up no 2026 pay item, board fight or governance proposal as of {checked}. The only nearby fact is the forfeited 2025 interim award (13G/A, Apr 2026), which is a past event.

items.label: Waiting to launch the retail voting program (SEC letter Sept 29)
Waiting on an equity raise (unlikely after the $30B credit lines)

deal_math._spcx_src: SpaceX 10-Q cover (Jul 28, 2026): 7,696,293,669 A + 5,485,486,276 B, plus 391,041,680 A issued in the Cursor merger (8-K Aug 14). Not a company-reported total.
deal_math._musk_votes_why: Derived. 424B4 beneficial ownership: Musk holds 849,494,440 A + 5,569,053,075 B (84.4% of votes, counting about 350M option shares). Outstanding-basis votes are about 10 x 5.219B B + 0.849B A ≈ 53.04B of about 62.94B total, which is ~84.3% and matches the 424B4 figure.
deal_math._musk_tsla_src: Schedule 13G/A filed Jun 16, 2026: 699,580,882 shares with voting rights. Excludes 423.7M award shares voted proportionally by proxy.
deal_math._vote_floor_why: Assumption: Tesla holders likely need $450 or more per share. Offers below that are treated as unlikely to pass.
deal_math.collar_note: An all-stock deal at a fixed ratio leaves Tesla holders exposed if SPCX falls before the vote. To win an independent Tesla vote it likely needs downside protection (a collar or price floor). SpaceX holders would resist, because it shifts value to Tesla holders if SPCX drops. This is general M&A practice, not deal-specific.
deal_math.reverse_note: Reverse case: Tesla acquires SpaceX. Tesla has one class of stock, so Musk's dual-class control would end. Shown for completeness; low probability.

close_timing._why: Used only once a letter or merger is detected (state = letter). Typical related-party all-stock steps; general practice, not rules.

steps.step: Negotiation to signed agreement (if it starts as a letter)
S-4 / joint proxy filed after signing
Special meeting after proxy mailing (Tesla's usual ~40-45 days)
HSR (30-day wait) / CFIUS / FCC (Starlink, spectrum): runs in parallel, a risk to close timing

Index preference: SPCX S&P 500 eligibility ~mid-2027 at the earliest (seasoning, unverified); outside estimates cite ~Sept 2027 and a clean ticker swap. Affects close-timing preference only, not near-term announcement odds.

secondary_markets._why: Shown in details only, as a sentiment gauge. The 2026 contracts were reported to have 'resolved No'. Not quite: Polymarket's Jun 30 and Sept 30, 2026 contracts resolved No, but Dec 31, 2026 is still open.

index_notes.label: Nasdaq-100 annual reconstitution, effective after the close Dec 18, 2026 (standard 3rd-Friday-of-December schedule; unverified for 2026)

S&P 500 eligibility for SPCX needs about 12 months of trading after the Jun 12, 2026 IPO, so ~Jun 2027 at the earliest. The 'Sept 2027' estimate and the Tesla-swap idea come from outside commentary; the seasoning rule wasn't re-checked for 2026 changes (unverified).

fcc_watch.note: The SpaceX-Grain transfer application was filed Oct 8 and asks for expedited consent. Its ECFS/ULS docket number wasn't found yet; the earlier T-Mobile to Grain proceeding was WT 25-178. The FCC's informal goal is 180 days for transaction review (general practice).

grain._why: SpaceX agreed on Oct 8, 2026 to buy Grain's 800 MHz licenses, pending FCC consent. While it's pending, merger odds in the next 14 days get x0.9 (a soft reason to sequence the deal after approval). On approval, the following 5 days get x1.2. Each run checks ECFS (Grain/SpaceX filers, proceeding 25-178) and Google News for approval wording. Detection is heuristic, so confirm by hand.

special_meeting_planned._why: If on, the merger vote is assumed to go to its own special meeting, so the e-proxy/Texas deadlines (urgency and timing anchors) stop pulling the merger letter forward. Letter timing uses plain weekday x calendar weights. The meeting-announcement ('either') curve is unchanged, and a letter only counts as 'meeting + merger' if it arrives by the time the meeting is announced. Result: merger-with-meeting falls and routine-only rises. Any letter that comes after the routine date belongs to the 2027 special-meeting path.

letter_after_kill._why: If a routine meeting is set with no SpaceX language, the 2026-meeting merger path is closed. Letter odds by mid-2027 are modeled as 0.6 x the pre-kill merger share: a clean routine proxy is evidence against a live deal, but a 2027 special meeting is still possible. This is judgment, not data. For comparison, Polymarket's Jun 30, 2027 contract is shown in details.

polymarket._why: Sentiment gauge only, not a base rate. These contracts ask whether a merger is 'officially announced', which is a different event from a meeting date, and they trade thinly.

blank_clock_source: Clock starts Mon Sept 21, 2026: the first Monday after the Sept 17 anniversary of last year's DEF 14A passed with no 2026 meeting date (Tesla's normal proxy timing). Sept 29 was considered and rejected.

path_separation._why: After Oct 26 a merger letter has likely missed this year's regular card. From Oct 27 on, each day's merger mass is (a) limited to the active-process share of the merger-hold reasons (the quiet-hold path, 'Musk asked the board to hold the date, no committee', doesn't respond to the notice deadline), and (b) decayed by exp(-0.005 x days after Oct 26). Routine keeps the full Texas/e-proxy deadline pressure. The removed merger mass is NOT redistributed to earlier weeks: it becomes a routine-date announcement on that same day plus a later merger letter (2027 special meeting path). Not applied when the special-meeting toggle is on (that toggle already decouples the letter from the card).

missed_card_switch._why: If no Tesla/SpaceX merger-related filing (statecheck state 'letter') exists by the close of Oct 26, 15% of the remaining meeting+merger weight moves to the 'letter later / special meeting (2027)' path. Auto-activates on the first run on/after Oct 27; armed before then.

rolloff._why: A day closes at 8 PM ET with no filing; its odds roll to the remaining open days (model conditions on no announcement so far). On a scheduled Tesla/SpaceX event day the day stays open until event_end_et (default start + 2.5h); an on-stage or X statement that night with an 8-K the next morning counts as that event day's announcement. After the event ends, the residual rolls to the next open morning.
